rationale: Both use the same sorted-layer decomposition and the 5+3 to 4+4 swap. B adds a second trade that is not valid: it turns a group of three plus a group of one into a group of four. After layering, the single-book group always holds the most frequent title, which is already in every other group, so merging produces a 'group of four' containing a duplicate title. For example, [1,1,2,3] should cost 2960 cents, but B returns 2560. That is a real correctness bug outside the tests. B also defines its own min, which shadows the Go 1.21 builtin. A's code is clear, it explains why the 5+3 swap is always a valid regrouping, it indexes the group counts uniformly in an array, and it avoids the bogus optimisation. A is clearly better.
